transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I've just been struggling a little bit lately. I feel terrible even admitting this out loud, because I know I should be trying harder, but I just... I don't really care about anything right now. 

It's like I've completely lost interest in all my normal activities. My art classes, the board-game nights I usually go to, hiking... I can't even get myself to care about getting back to the soccer team. I mostly just end up sitting in my room while everything kind of slips away from me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds awful, like I'm just being lazy or something. But... is that the kind of information you needed to know?
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

Um, well... it's kind of just been this one really long stretch, actually. I've never really felt quite like this before in my life. It started... gosh, I feel a little silly admitting this, because I know I should be handling things better by now, but it started shortly after my divorce. 

That was about a year and eleven months ago. So it's been going on for almost two years now. I've been trying really hard to push through it, I promise, it's just been a bit stubborn. I hope it's okay that I mentioned the divorce... I just wanted to give you the exact timeline. Is that the right kind of information for you?
During these past two years, have there been any specific periods where your mood and energy dropped significantly lower than your current baseline, making it difficult to function at all?

Um... I really hate to admit this, because it makes me sound so incapable, and I really have been trying my best to keep up with things. But... yeah, I guess it did drop lower. 

Around the following summer after the divorce... it just kind of became this constant thing. It hasn't really lifted since then, so it's been about a year and four months of it just being... well, there all the time. I know I should have reached out for help sooner instead of just letting it go on for a year and four months like that without getting a handle on it. I'm really sorry. 

Am I answering your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
